items.question: Which command shows the folder you are in right now?
items.explanation: pwd means print working directory. It shows the full path of the current folder.

items.question: What does cd .. do?
items.explanation: Two dots mean the folder above. One dot means the current folder, and ~ means your home folder.

items.question: Type the command that creates an empty file named style.css.
items.explanation: touch creates an empty file. (On PowerShell, use ni.)
items.hint: It sounds like you are touching the file.

items.question: Which key finishes a file or folder name for you?
items.explanation: Tab completes names. It saves typing and avoids spelling mistakes, because it only completes names that really exist.

items.question: What does the -a option of ls show?
options: Hidden files (names starting with a dot)
items.explanation: ls -a shows all files, including hidden ones such as .gitignore and the .git folder.

items.question: Which command deletes a folder and everything inside it?
items.explanation: rm -r removes recursively, so the folder and all its contents are deleted. Without -r, rm refuses to delete a folder.

items.question: Why must you be careful with rm?
options: It deletes forever, with no recycle bin
It copies files to the internet
items.explanation: The terminal has no recycle bin. Check with ls first, and read your command twice.

items.question: Which command renames old.html to new.html?
items.explanation: mv moves a file. In the same folder, moving is the same as renaming.

items.question: Which keys stop a command that is still running in the terminal?
items.explanation: Ctrl + C interrupts the running command. It is also how you stop a local server.

items.question: The terminal says: command not found. What does it usually mean?
options: The command is misspelled, or the tool is not installed
items.explanation: Check the spelling first. If it is correct, the tool may not be installed or may not be in your PATH.

items.question: A Python error message has several lines. Which line usually tells you the type and the cause of the problem?
options: The last line, such as NameError: name 'x' is not defined
items.explanation: Read an error from the bottom. The last line names the type of error and says what is wrong. The lines above show where.

items.question: Which shortcut opens the command palette, where you can search every VS Code command?
items.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + P (Cmd + Shift + P on macOS) is the command palette. If you forget a shortcut, search here.

items.question: Which browser tool tab shows JavaScript errors?
items.explanation: Press F12 and open the Console tab. Errors appear in red, with the file name and the line number.

items.question: What does the Live Server extension do?
options: Hosts your site on the internet for everyone
Opens your page in the browser and reloads it when you save
items.explanation: Live Server runs a local server and refreshes the browser each time you save. It is only on your computer.

items.question: Which search is most likely to find help for an error?
options: The exact error message plus the language, such as: python NameError name is not defined
items.explanation: Copy the exact error message, add the language or tool, and open results from official documentation or trusted sites.
